

=== How Europe and China fund open source — chapter with conclusions — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/funding/ ===

# Chapter — How Europe and China fund open source

*Version 1.0, 3 November 2026. Closes research branches R12–R15 (docs/RESEARCH-REGISTER.md) for this round. Later rounds produce new versions of this chapter; changes are listed at the end.*

> **Open-source research from public sources, not official statistics.** Incomplete and correctable. Absence of data means *we found nothing*, not that nothing exists. Contribute: GitHub issues (label `funding-data`) or contact@eu-china-commons.eu.

Labels: **[F]** fact (sourced, evidence A/B) · **[C]** commitment (announced, not shown as spent) · **[I]** inference · **[P]** proposal.

## 1. What we measured
| Component | Records | Source file |
|---|---|---|
| Public money, open-source-specific only | EU 24, CN 21 (+ excluded generic schemes logged) | data/funding/, docs/FUNDING-COMPARISON.md |
| Private corporate money via foundations | EU 23 (Eclipse, FSFE, KDE, TDF…), CN OpenAtom 2020–23 | same, §1a |
| Modalities (who decides, instruments, strings) | qualitative fields on all records | docs/FUNDING-MODALITIES.md |
| Funding of individual projects | 34 projects (18 CN-origin, 16 EU) | docs/PROJECT-FUNDING.md, data/project-funding.json |

Amounts in EUR at ECB annual average rates. Depth reached: centres 2–3, peripheries 1–2 (docs/RESEARCH-DEPTH.md).

## 2. Findings

### 2.1 Amounts
1. **[F]** Documented EU public open-source money that can be summed: €11.5M (2023), €36M (2024), €19M (2025) — Germany and France only. On top, multi-year EU envelopes **[C]**: DARE up to €120M, NGI Zero ≈€65.5M (2018–27), OpenEuroLLM €20.6M, Chips JU RISC-V €60M.
2. **[F]** No Chinese public open-source amount could be summed: China publishes **per-project caps and rates**, not budgets or disbursements (largest caps: Wuhan East Lake ¥30M, Shanghai ¥20M, Shenzhen ¥10M). **[F]** No central-government open-source budget line was found.
3. **[F]** OpenAtom, China's national open-source foundation, filed ¥270M of income 2020–23 (≈€9–10M/yr in donations), 100% domestic, Huawei 37% (2023), plus ¥20.7M of government subsidy in 2023. **[I]** The widely cited "¥600M+ since 2020" (Xinhua) is not supported by the filings.
4. **[F]** European private corporate money is fragmented and small where it can be isolated (FSFE + KDE ≈€0.1–0.2M/yr); Eclipse Foundation (Belgium) has €9.4–15.4M revenue (2022–25) but does not separate member fees from public grants. **[I]** With Eclipse as an upper bound, European foundation money is of the same order as OpenAtom.

### 2.2 Modalities
5. **[F]/[I]** **China pays for adoption; Europe pays for creation and maintenance.** Chinese instruments are local adoption subsidies (Shenzhen 15% of investment + 5% for OpenHarmony-adapted RISC-V), prize-style grants paid after deployment, per-device rates. European instruments are competitive grants for new strategic tech (RISC-V, LLMs), small grants via intermediaries (NLnet), and — uniquely in Germany — a standing maintenance fund (Sovereign Tech Fund: curl €195k, OpenSSL €406k, KDE €1.29M).
6. **[F]** **Chinese money is tied to named national stacks** (OpenHarmony, openEuler, RISC-V, OpenAtom-hosted projects) and local registration; **European money is stack-neutral** and conditioned on open licences and co-funding. **[I]** In practice Chinese instruments exclude foreign firms; European ones do not exclude anyone by nationality.
7. **[F]** **Who decides:** in China local industry bureaus and development zones (the centre acts through OpenAtom, under MIIT supervision); in Europe the Commission's programmes and a few national agencies. The EU periphery (member states) is mostly absent: 23 of 27 show no dedicated money in our search **[I: light search, not conclusive]**.

### 2.3 Projects
8. **[F]/[I]** **Chinese flagships depend on one company each** (Huawei for OpenHarmony/openEuler; Alibaba, Baidu, Tencent, Ant, PingCAP, High-Flyer…), with the top funder close to 100%; Chinese-origin projects at Apache keep the founding company as payer. **European projects have more diverse, multinational funders** and are paid mostly by subscriptions or dual licensing (Nextcloud, Qt, SUSE, Element), with grants and donations for maintenance (curl, GnuPG, KDE, OpenSSL).
9. **[F]** Individual donations are almost absent in China (Ant Design ≈US$18k all-time on Open Collective; KubeSphere 0) versus e.g. curl ≈US$91k/yr.
10. **[F]** Governments as **paying customers** of open-source vendors are a European channel (BSI VS-Desktop for GnuPG, BwMessenger/Tchap for Element, openDesk); the closest Chinese equivalent is 信创 procurement of commercial openEuler distributions, which buys the proprietary product layer, not the commons. **[F]** Part of OpenAtom's project money flows back to the main donor (¥6.49M of ¥25.8M OpenHarmony spending to Huawei Cloud, 2023).

### 2.4 Transparency
11. **[F]** The transparency gap is the largest asymmetry found: European budgets and grants are published per project; Chinese support is visible as rules and ceilings, and award notices are scattered across local portals. **[I]** Any headline "China spends X vs Europe Y" is today unfounded in both directions.

## 3. Limits of this round
- Peripheries under-researched: EU national budgets not read; Chinese provincial portals not swept one by one; Chinese award notices (拟资助名单) not collected.
- Contributor-employer shares mostly inferred (B/C); OpenDigger affiliation data pulled for one project only.
- OCR-derived OpenAtom figures to be re-read on page images; several European figures (SCS, GnuPG STF, Matrix.org) to confirm.
- Exchange rates: annual averages; multi-year envelopes converted at start year.

## 4. Implications for EU–China cooperation **[P]**
1. **Complementarity is real and measurable:** China funds adoption at scale, Europe funds maintenance and creation. A shared agenda on **maintenance of common upstreams** (projects both sides depend on: Linux, OpenSSL, curl, RISC-V toolchains, Apache projects of Chinese origin) is non-competitive and verifiable.
2. **Transparency as the first cooperation deliverable:** a common, open template for reporting public open-source funding (amount, instrument, project, disbursement) — the schema used here could be the starting point.
3. **Diversify funding of Chinese-origin global projects:** single-company dependence is a resilience risk for everyone using them; European maintenance funds and foundations could co-fund under open governance.
4. **Screen, don't exclude:** OpenAtom is a state-supervised, single-country-funded vehicle; engagement should go through neutral foundations (Eclipse, Apache, OpenChain) with economic-security screening, as already practised in Oniro and Catena-X.

## 5. Next rounds (re-run recipes in RESEARCH-REGISTER R12–R15)
Chinese award notices (Shenzhen, Shanghai, Wuhan, Hangzhou, Guangdong); national budgets of the 10 largest EU economies; Eclipse Belgian statutory accounts; OpenDigger affiliation for openEuler, OpenHarmony, MindSpore, PaddlePaddle; OpenAtom 2024–25 filings when published.

## Changelog
- v1.0 (3 Nov 2026): first closure of the funding chapter.


=== Funding for open source: EU vs China, comparison tables in EUR — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/funding-data/ ===

# Funding for open source — EU vs China (public money and private corporate money)

*Generated by tools/build_funding.js on 2026-11-08. Do not edit by hand.*

> **Open-source research, not official statistics.** These figures are collected from publicly available sources (budgets, programme pages, official filings, press) by the Europe–China Digital Commons Observatory. They are incomplete, may contain errors, and compare instruments that are not always equivalent. Absence of a jurisdiction means *we found nothing*, not that it spends nothing.
>
> **Help us improve them:** open an issue on GitHub (https://github.com/fpietrosanti/eu-china-commons/issues/new?labels=funding-data&title=Funding%20data%3A%20) or write to contact@eu-china-commons.eu. Please include the source (link, document, page) for any correction or addition.

## Method
- Amounts kept in the original currency and converted to EUR at the **ECB annual average rate** of the record's year (ECB SDW series EXR/A.CNY.EUR.SP00.A (annual average, CNY per 1 EUR)). Rates used: 2020: 7.8747, 2021: 7.6282, 2022: 7.0788, 2023: 7.66, 2024: 7.7875, 2025: 8.1185 CNY/EUR.
- **Totals include only `summable` records**: disbursed or budgeted, annual, open-source-specific. Multi-year envelopes are shown separately and annualised for reference only. Per-project caps are never summed.
- Evidence levels A–D as in docs/METHODOLOGY.md §4. Fact = disbursed/budgeted with a source; commitment = envelope or announcement.

## 1. Public money: annual totals (summable records only, EUR)

| Year | EU | China | CN/EU |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 11.5 M | not documented | n/a |
| 2024 | 36.0 M | not documented | n/a |
| 2025 | 19.0 M | not documented | n/a |
| 2026 | not documented | 2.6 M | n/a |

*Inference warning: the totals reflect what is documented, which is much more for the EU (published budgets) than for China (caps and envelopes dominate).*

## 1a. Private corporate money via foundations and company programmes (summable records only, EUR)

| Year | EU | China | CN/EU |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 77 k | 2.0 M | 26.56 |
| 2021 | 137 k | 9.0 M | 65.73 |
| 2022 | 149 k | 9.0 M | 60.42 |
| 2023 | 173 k | 9.9 M | 56.92 |
| 2024 | 168 k | not documented | n/a |

*Never added to public money. China: OpenAtom filed donation income; EU: European foundations' corporate income (membership, donations, sponsorship). Donor nationality matters: see the records' notes.*

Grants (*fondo perduto*), adoption subsidies and tax credits for firms adopting strategic national open-source technologies are in scope; when only a rate or a cap is published they are listed but not summed.

> **Open-source research, not official statistics.** These figures are collected from publicly available sources (budgets, programme pages, official filings, press) by the Europe–China Digital Commons Observatory. They are incomplete, may contain errors, and compare instruments that are not always equivalent. Absence of a jurisdiction means *we found nothing*, not that it spends nothing.
>
> **Help us improve them:** open an issue on GitHub (https://github.com/fpietrosanti/eu-china-commons/issues/new?labels=funding-data&title=Funding%20data%3A%20) or write to contact@eu-china-commons.eu. Please include the source (link, document, page) for any correction or addition.


=== How each side funds open source for sovereignty: modalities compared — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/funding-modalities/ ===

# How China and Europe fund open source for sovereignty — qualitative analysis

*Draft frame, 3 Nov 2026. Filled from data/funding/{eu,cn}.json (qualitative fields) and the catalogue. Claims labelled fact / commitment / inference / proposal.*

> Open-source research from public sources; incomplete and correctable. Contribute: GitHub issues (label `funding-data`) or contact@eu-china-commons.eu.

## 1. Questions
1. **Who decides and who manages the money?** (ministry, agency, foundation, SOE, local bureau, EDIC)
2. **Through which instruments?** direct spending, grants, adoption subsidies, tax credits, procurement, donations via foundations.
3. **What is funded: creation, adoption or maintenance?**
4. **With which strings?** national stack, local registration, licence, security review, upstream contribution.
5. **With which sovereignty narrative?** 自主可控 / 安全可靠 / 信创 / 国产替代 vs digital sovereignty / strategic autonomy / public money public code.
6. **How open to the other side?** foreign contributors, foreign firms, international upstreams.
7. **How accountable?** published budgets, disbursement data, evaluation.

## 2. Comparison grid (first fill, 3 Nov 2026: 24 EU + 21 CN records)
| Dimension | China | EU (institutions) | EU member states |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main funders | Local industry bureaus and development-zone committees (Shenzhen, Shanghai, Wuhan East Lake, Hangzhou, Guangdong, Jiangsu); centre acts via OpenAtom (MIIT-supervised, funded by corporate donations, 100% domestic 2022–23), **no central open-source budget line found** | Commission programmes and joint undertakings: Horizon/NGI, Digital Europe, Chips JU, EuroHPC; DC-EDIC (small, mostly in kind) | Germany (Sovereign Tech Agency, ZenDiS, Prototype Fund) and France (DINUM, BlueHats) only; 23 states: nothing found (light search) |
| Dominant instrument | Prize-style grants paid after results; **adoption subsidies as % of investment** (Shenzhen 15% + 5% RISC-V; Wuhan 50% of R&D); per-device rates; venture-style fund matrices (Jiangsu) | Competitive grants, cascade funding through intermediaries (NLnet small grants) | Agency contracts for maintenance (DE); in-house development (DE openDesk, FR La Suite); small prizes (FR) |
| Stage funded | **Adoption and commercialisation** (distributions, native apps, devices); some creation (Shanghai tools, Hangzhou incubation); maintenance only in Guangdong (30% of community operating costs) | **Creation** of strategic tech (RISC-V/DARE, OpenEuroLLM) and small new projects (NGI) | **Adoption by public bodies** (openDesk, La Suite) and **maintenance** (Sovereign Tech Fund, unique in Europe) |
| Selection | Yearly local calls with review panels; awards after certification/sales/deployment | Open competitive calls; NLnet rolling open calls | Agency selection of critical projects (STA); open calls (Prototype Fund) |
| Conditions | Local registration; use of a named domestic stack (OpenHarmony, RISC-V, OpenAtom-hosted / "national open-source organisation"); payment tied to results | Open licence (NGI); co-funding (DARE, Chips JU) | Open licence; no domestic-firm requirement found |
| Sovereignty frame | Not explicit in the texts read (no 自主可控 quote found yet) — **to check** | "strategic autonomy", "digital sovereignty" in programme texts (to quote) | "digital sovereignty" (ZenDiS, STA) — to quote; "public money, public code" not found in sources |
| Openness to foreign participants | Never stated; local-registration and domestic-stack conditions exclude foreign firms in practice (inference) | Mostly unclear; NGI open to applicants worldwide (to verify) | Unclear; STA funds global upstream projects regardless of maintainers' nationality (to verify) |
| Transparency of amounts | **Only caps and rates published**; no adopted budget or disbursement found; award notices (拟资助名单) not yet collected | Envelopes published (CORDIS, calls) | Annual budgets published (DE), cumulative figures (FR) |

## 2b. First reading of the hypotheses (inference, 3 Nov)
- H1 (CN adoption vs EU creation/maintenance): **supported** by the first fill.
- H2 (CN foundations + local policy vs EU agencies): **supported**; the absence of any central budget line in China is notable.
- H3 (CN tied to named stacks, EU stack-neutral): **supported**.
- H4 (transparency asymmetry): **strongly supported**: 0 summable CN records vs 5 EU.
- H5 (different sovereignty goals): **not yet testable** — the sovereignty phrases still have to be quoted from the texts on both sides.
- Caveat: the EU side is dominated by DE and FR; 23 member states and the national budgets were not read; Chinese portals were not swept one by one.

## 3. Working hypotheses (inference, to test against the data)
- H1. China funds **adoption** of a few national stacks (openEuler, OpenHarmony, RISC-V) through local industrial subsidies and caps; Europe funds **creation and maintenance** of many independent projects through grants (NGI, Sovereign Tech Agency).
- H2. In China the money flows through **foundation donations from large firms** (OpenAtom: 100% domestic donations, 2022–2023) plus **local government industrial policy**; in Europe through **public agencies and EU programmes**.
- H3. Chinese instruments are tied to **named domestic stacks**; European ones are mostly **stack-neutral** but tied to licence/openness conditions.
- H4. Transparency is asymmetric: European budgets are published; Chinese support is mostly visible as **rates and caps**, not totals.
- H5. Both sides use **sovereignty** language, but with different goals: replacement of foreign technology (China) vs reducing dependency while staying in global upstreams (EU).

## 4. Implications for cooperation (proposal, after the data)


=== How 34 major open-source projects are funded (EU and China) — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/project-funding/ ===

# How major open-source projects are funded — Europe vs China

*3 Nov 2026. 34 projects (18 Chinese or Chinese-origin, 16 European). Data: `data/project-funding.json`. Every channel claim is labelled fact or inference, with an evidence level (docs/METHODOLOGY.md §4).*

> Open-source research from public sources; incomplete and correctable. Contribute: GitHub issues (label `funding-data`) or contact@eu-china-commons.eu.

## Method
- Channels per project: (a) employer-paid developers, (b) foundation budget, (c) public grants, (d) corporate sponsorship/membership, (e) commercial model, (f) individual donations.
- Reused, not re-researched: OpenAtom 2021–23 accounts (docs/CN-FOUNDATIONS.md), local subsidies (data/funding/cn.json), STF/NGI/EuroHPC/KDE/TDF records (data/funding/eu.json).
- New in this pass: Open Collective GraphQL amounts (curl, Ant Design, KubeSphere), Sovereign Tech Fund per-project amounts (curl, OpenSSL, KDE), OpenDigger contributor activity (Apache Doris).
- Contributor affiliation is mostly **inference** (C/B) from project ownership; a systematic OpenDigger/Gitee affiliation pass is still to be done.

| KubeSphere | Open Collective US$0 | opencollective.com |

## EU vs CN patterns — findings
1. **FACT (A).** The two Chinese state-flagship projects (OpenHarmony, openEuler) are financed through one channel stack: an anchor company (Huawei) that writes the code, OpenAtom as foundation budget (itself 37% Huawei-funded in 2023), and local adoption subsidies that pay *users* to deploy them. Part of the foundation money returns to the donor (¥6.49M to Huawei Cloud).
2. **INFERENCE (B).** Every other Chinese project in the sample is single-company: Alibaba (Qwen, Dubbo, RocketMQ, Anolis), Baidu (Paddle, ECharts), Tencent (OpenCloudOS), Ant (Ant Design), PingCAP, API7, LangGenius, QingCloud, High-Flyer (DeepSeek). Concentration on the top funder is near-total.
3. **FACT (A/B).** Chinese projects show almost no individual-donation channel: Ant Design ~US$18k all-time, KubeSphere US$0, none for the others found. curl alone collected US$499k on Open Collective.
4. **INFERENCE (B).** Chinese-origin Apache projects (Doris, ECharts, Dubbo, RocketMQ, APISIX) use the ASF for neutral governance and global reach, but the money is still the founding Chinese company or its VC-funded spin-off; the ASF pays no developers.
5. **FACT/INFERENCE (B).** European projects are more mixed: commercial subscriptions or dual licensing (Nextcloud, Qt, SUSE, Open-Xchange, Element) carry most of the engineering, with small public grants (STF, NGI) and donations covering maintenance gaps (curl, KDE, OpenSSL, GnuPG).
6. **FACT (A).** European public money for named projects is mostly *creation* via large envelopes (OpenEuroLLM €20.6M, DARE €120M) or *maintenance* via STF (€0.2–1.3M per project). Chinese public money in the sample is mostly *adoption* (subsidies to deploy OpenHarmony/openEuler) and state labs (XiangShan/CAS, Peng Cheng/MindSpore).
7. **INFERENCE (C).** The European government-as-customer model is a distinct funding channel: GnuPG (BSI VS-Desktop), Element (BwMessenger, Tchap), openDesk components (Nextcloud, Collabora, Open-Xchange). It has no clear Chinese counterpart in this sample except Xinchuang procurement of commercial openEuler distributions.
8. **FACT (B).** Funder nationality is domestic on both sides for the flagships (OpenAtom donations 100% domestic 2022–23), but European projects draw on cross-border funders (US sponsors of curl/OpenSSL, Google/Valve for KDE, Sweden-owned SUSE, foreign VC in Mistral).
9. **FACT (B).** Licences diverge at the edges: MulanPSL-2.0 for openEuler/XiangShan; source-available drift at Dify and KubeSphere (CN), and at Mistral (some weights) and Qt (dual licence) in Europe.

## Gaps / next steps
- Contributor affiliation from OpenDigger/Gitee for openEuler, OpenHarmony, MindSpore, Paddle (would turn inference C into B/A on employer shares).
- Verify SCS BMWK grant amount and GnuPG STF amount; Matrix.org Foundation accounts (UK filings).


=== The Chinese open-source landscape: projects and code platforms — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/china-open-source-landscape/ ===

# Chinese open-source landscape: most relevant and most used projects

Research note, 3 Nov 2026. Scope: (1) the most influential and most used open-source projects that originate in China, (2) how Chinese developers use their own code platforms (Gitee, AtomGit/GitCode) compared with GitHub. Evidence levels follow `docs/METHODOLOGY.md` §4. This note adds to the `industrial-stack` records in `data/catalogue-verified.json` (openEuler, OpenHarmony, OpenAnolis, XiangShan, PaddlePaddle, DeepSeek, Qwen, OpenAtom, AtomGit) and does not repeat them. Those projects appear below (marked *) only so the other rows can be ranked against them.

**Metric caveat.** Stars measure attention, not deployment. OpenRank (X-lab) measures collaboration influence from GitHub activity, so it under-counts work hosted on Gitee and AtomGit. Neither metric counts installs. We found no primary-source download or install figures in this pass; that gap is listed in §4.

Source keys:
- **[GH]** GitHub REST API `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}`, fetched 2026-11-03. Level A (we measured it on the platform).
- **[GE]** Gitee API v5 `https://gitee.com/api/v5/repos/{owner}/{repo}`, fetched 2026-11-03. `gvp`=true means the repo is a Gitee Most Valuable Project. Counts are level A; GVP is an editorial label from the platform.
- **[OD]** OpenDigger `https://oss.x-lab.info/open_digger/github/{owner}/{repo}/openrank.json`, 2024 annual value, fetched 2026-11-03. Level A (primary dataset; method by X-lab).
- **[COSR25]** *2025 China Open Source Annual Report* (KAIYUANSHE/开源社), published 22 Jun 2026. We read its tables as reported by IT之家, `https://www.ithome.com/0/968/251.htm`, fetched 2026-11-03. Level B: a press relay, and we have not yet read the original at https://kaiyuanshe.github.io/. It moves to A once we do.

Next come PingCAP, Espressif, Tencent, FIT2CLOUD, DaoCloud, SelectDB, LobeHub, Zilliz, openKylin and StarRocks [COSR25, 2025, B].

## 2. Gitee vs AtomGit vs GitHub

| Platform | Claimed / measured size | Source, date | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub (Chinese users) | >2.1 m active Chinese developers at end-2025, #3 worldwide after the US (5.08 m) and India (2.55 m) | COSR25 via ithome.com/0/968/251.htm, 2026-06 | B |
| All platforms (Chinese estimate) | >3.5 m Chinese developers once Gitee, AtomGit and GitCode are counted (#2 worldwide) | same | B (an estimate made inside the report) |
| Gitee | "14 million developers" (1400万的开发者) | https://gitee.com/about_us, fetched 2026-11-03 | C (self-reported) |
| AtomGit (merged with GitCode, Oct 2025) | 10.87 m developers at end-Apr 2026; "1000+ 万" at end-Feb 2026 | https://gitcode.csdn.net/6a6872d510ee7a33f2935e66.html (operator's monthly report); https://docs.gitcode.com/en/docs/help/home/aboutus/ | C (self-reported by the operator, CSDN) |
| Repo counts | No primary source found in this pass | - | gap |

Gitee and AtomGit report registered accounts (10–14 m). GitHub's figure (2.1 m) counts active developers. The definitions differ, so the numbers cannot be compared directly.

## 3. Findings

1. **Fact (B).** OpenHarmony is the #1 open-source project worldwide by OpenRank 2025 (60,089, about 1.5x Azure), and openEuler is #10. Both are OpenAtom Foundation projects seeded by Huawei. [COSR25]
2. **Fact (B).** Huawei is the #2 company worldwide by OpenRank 2025 (89,369), behind Microsoft (205,597), and has the most active repos (8,273) of any company in the global Top 15. The Chinese company layer is highly concentrated: Huawei alone scores more than the next four Chinese firms combined (75,305). [COSR25]
3. **Inference.** China's OpenRank weight comes mainly from state-aligned operating-system stacks hosted by foundations. The US list, by contrast, is led by developer-tooling and cloud projects. This matches the "OS + AI models" pattern recorded in `INDUSTRIAL-STACKS.md`.
4. **Fact (B).** Qwen has 20% of downloads of models above 1B parameters (Meta 23.2%, DeepSeek 3.8%). The report also says Chinese open models overtook US models in Hugging Face downloads in summer 2025, and that AI is the fastest-growing domain (repos growing more than 210% a year). [COSR25]
5. **Fact (A).** The China-originated projects with the most GitHub stars in Nov 2026 are AI application layers (Dify 160k, DeepSeek-V3 105k, RAGFlow 93k) and established frontend kits (Ant Design 100k, ECharts 68k). [GH]
6. **Fact (B) + inference.** Chinese-led projects draw mostly on Chinese contributors: 79.14% of contributions to China-led projects come from inside China, against 38.21% domestic contributions for US-led projects. China ranks 10th for internationalisation. Inference: EU contributors have few working ties to these projects. That limits how far EU actors can help govern Chinese commons, and the same holds in the other direction. [COSR25]
7. **Fact (A) + inference.** The most-starred Gitee-native projects (Sa-Token, Pig, RuoYi-Vue, Hutool, JeecgBoot) are Java back-office scaffolds and enterprise utilities, with very high fork counts (Pig: 13,417 forks). Inference: Gitee is where Chinese enterprise and government-contractor application development happens. GitHub-based OpenRank does not see this layer. [GE]
8. **Fact (A).** Many flagship infrastructure projects of Chinese origin have been donated to the Apache Software Foundation (Doris, ECharts, Dubbo, RocketMQ, APISIX, ShardingSphere). Their governance is therefore foreign or neutral even where the main vendor is Chinese. At project level, this is the main existing channel for commons shared between the EU and China (see catalogue record `xx-apache-china-projects`). [GH]

## 4. Gaps / next steps
- Read the KAIYUANSHE 2024 and 2025 reports directly (kaiyuanshe.github.io; hackmd.io/@2024COSR) to raise COSR25 to level A and add its Top lists of Chinese projects by domain.
- Not fetched in this pass (budget): the full Gitee GVP list, the Gitee annual report, the AtomGit G-Star list, the CAICT open-source white paper and the OSCHINA yearly top projects.
- Find install/download metrics (Maven Central, npm, PyPI, Hugging Face) for rows 4–28.


=== Chinese open-source foundations and OpenAtom finances — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/chinese-foundations/ ===

# Chinese open-source foundations and bodies: governance, priorities, finances

Research note, 2026-11-03. Evidence levels per METHODOLOGY.md §4. Self-reported figures are C unless they come from an official filing.

## 1. OpenAtom Open Source Foundation (开放原子开源基金会)
- **Governance.** National non-profit foundation, founded June 2020, registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs, supervised by **MIIT**. Founding donors: Alibaba, Baidu, Huawei, Inspur, Qihoo 360, Tencent, China Merchants Bank. Donors sit in four tiers. Sources: https://huanqiu.com/article/45RxvLVHOas (B); https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%BC%80%E6%94%BE%E5%8E%9F%E5%AD%90%E5%BC%80%E6%BA%90%E5%9F%BA%E9%87%91%E4%BC%9A/53481350 (C).
- **Information disclosure.** Annual work reports for 2020–2023 are listed at https://openatom.cn/information/work (A, page). The 2022 and 2023 PDFs are **image-only scans**: pdftotext returned no text. We need OCR before we can extract the financials. We found no 2024 or 2025 report on that page.
- **Finances.**
  - More than **CNY 600 million raised cumulatively since 2020**. Xinhua, 25 Jun 2026, https://www.news.cn/info/20260625/a9b84c78ac8946c6a7e37bbae91513af/c.html. Self-reported via press: **C**.
  - **198 donor organisations**, of which 55 are platinum, gold or silver. 9 new unrestricted donors in 2026. 12 project donations renewed (same source, C).
  - We found no audited breakdown of income or spending.
- **Projects.**
  - 2020: 7 founding projects, including OpenHarmony and XuperChain. https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/234694705 (C)
  - Jul 2025: more than 60 projects passed TOC admission, 41 in incubation, 8 newly donated (AI, embodied intelligence, blockchain). http://www.news.cn/sci-tech/20250725/fad2cf09702c410985ce5318d5c587cf/c.html (B)
  - 2025 report: 52 projects in incubation. **OpenHarmony and openEuler graduated.** OpenHarmony: more than 10k contributors, more than 1,500 certified products. openEuler: more than 24k contributors, more than 16m installs. https://dpiche.com/index/archives/81.html (third-party relay of the report, C)
  - Jun 2026: 58 projects in 18 fields. 6 new projects: xLLM, JoySafety, openSupOS, OpenLET, 电鸿 IoT OS, LoongArch binary translator. Mulan licence family donated (Mulan PSL v2 is OSI-approved; reported in use by more than 330k projects). Xinhua 2026 (B)
- **Priorities by year.**
  - 2020–22: OS, blockchain, basic software.
  - 2024: developers + academia (首届开源技术学术大会).
  - 2025: "全栈协同"; AI, quantum, BCI, embodied intelligence.
  - 2026: AI agents, LoongArch/chips, robotics, industrial control.
- **Other output.** 《中国开源发展深度报告（2025）》, compiled by the OpenAtom secretariat, June 2025: https://www.163.com/dy/article/L0J5CCN50511B8LM.html (B)

## 2. KAIYUANSHE (开源社)
- **Governance.** A volunteer community founded in 2014, with an elected board (理事会), working groups and a finance group. We found no registered legal entity or 年检 record (verify). Funding comes from corporate sponsorship of COSCon plus small donations. Source: 2021 annual report https://kaiyuanshe.github.io/document/kys-report-2021/2021%20%E5%BC%80%E6%BA%90%E7%A4%BE%E5%B9%B4%E5%BA%A6%E6%8A%A5%E5%91%8A.pdf (A for the text; figures C).
- **FY2021 finances** (self-reported, C):

| Item | CNY |
|---|---|
| Carry-forward from FY20 (bank 409,247 + Alipay 20,414) | 429,661 |
| Sponsorship programme | 556,000 (of which 312,000 pending) |
| Public donations | 43,000 |
| COSCon tickets | 5,062 |
| **Total income** | **604,062** |

| Operations / tax / fees | 14,685 |
| COSCon'21 sponsorship receivable | 868,000 (676,000 received) |
| Foreign donation | Near Foundation, USD 6,246 |

  The report itself flags missing reimbursement rules; budgeting was planned for 2022.
- **Priorities.** COSCon, the 中国开源年度报告 (published since 2015), open-source education, open-source risk governance, international links (ASF, Near). See COSCON-THEMES.md.
- **Gap.** We have not yet fetched the FY2022–FY2025 annual reports. They are probably at kaiyuanshe.github.io/document/kys-report-20XX/.

## 3. COPU (中国开源软件推进联盟, China OSS Promotion Union)
- **Governance.** An industry alliance chaired by **Lu Shouqun (陆首群)**, who runs regular meetings (例会). Vice-chair Liu Peng (刘澎). Members: companies, universities and institutes. Sources: https://cosspu.org.cn/osinfo/shownews.php?id=277 (A, minutes 2025-07-08); http://copu-oss.org.cn/download/ (A).
- **Output.**
  - The annual **中国开源发展蓝皮书** (2021–2025), compiled by the Beijing Open Source Innovation Committee with CSDN, OpenAtom, CCID, ISCAS and others, published on GitCode: https://gitcode.net/COPU/2023 , https://gitcode.com/choss_skw/2025book (A).
  - 《2024中国开源发展现状》, released 2025-02-13 (A, download page).
  - Liu Peng's 2022 claim that China is "near world level in some fields": https://blog.csdn.net/csdnopensource/article/details/125943982 (B).
- **Finances.** Nothing public found (gap).

## 4. CCF ODC (CCF开源发展委员会)
- A committee of the China Computer Federation. It reportedly focuses on academic open source (GitLink platform, 开源之夏 summer programme). We could not verify the founding date or chair this pass: **D, lead only**.

## 5. CAICT, LF APAC/China, OSCHINA/Gitee
- CAICT and Gitee/OSCHINA are already registered in data/stakeholders.json; nothing new this pass. LF APAC/China was not researched (budget).

## 6. Comparison

| Body | Type | Controller / funder | Money (best figure) | Flagship output | Ev. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAtom | public foundation, MIIT-supervised | big-tech donors (Huawei, Alibaba, Tencent…) + state guidance | more than CNY 600m raised 2020–mid-2026 | OpenHarmony, openEuler (graduated); 58 projects | C (money), B (projects) |
| KAIYUANSHE | volunteer community | corporate COSCon sponsors | CNY 0.60m income (FY21) | COSCon, 中国开源年度报告 | C |
| COPU | industry alliance | members | n/a | 中国开源发展蓝皮书 | A (outputs) |
| CCF ODC | professional-society committee | CCF | n/a | 开源之夏, GitLink | D |
| CAICT | MIIT think tank | state | n/a | OSCAR certification, white papers | B (registry) |

## 7. Findings
1. **FACT (C/B).** OpenAtom holds most of the money in Chinese open source. The roughly CNY 600m it reports for 2020–26 is about 1,000 times KAIYUANSHE's CNY 0.6m FY21 income.
2. **FACT (B).** OpenAtom's portfolio follows industrial-policy priorities: OS, LoongArch, chips, embodied AI, industrial control. Its 2026 conference coverage does not mention international cooperation.
3. **FACT (A).** KAIYUANSHE is the community-side actor with international ties: it co-ran COSCon'20 with the ASF and received a Near Foundation donation in 2021. It publishes detailed but unaudited finances.
4. **FACT (B).** OpenAtom now stewards the Mulan licence family, which includes the OSI-approved Mulan PSL v2. That makes it a concrete counterpart for EU licence work (EUPL compatibility).
5. **INFERENCE.** Disclosure is weak. OpenAtom's work reports are scanned images and stop at 2023 online, which limits verifiable comparison. Next steps: OCR, and the 民政部 慈善中国 / 社会组织 registry from a CN IP.
6. **INFERENCE.** For EU–China cooperation, the low-risk entry points are community and academic: KAIYUANSHE/COSCon and CCF ODC 开源之夏 alongside EU OSPO networks and Eclipse/ASF. Engaging OpenAtom means engaging an MIIT-supervised industrial-policy vehicle, which needs economic-security screening.
7. **INFERENCE.** Both sides have converged on AI open source (COSCon'25 "Open Intelligence"; OpenAtom's AI-agent datasets). That makes open-source AI governance and licensing the likeliest shared agenda.

## 8. Open items
- OCR the OpenAtom 2020–2023 work-report PDFs (copies on the server at /tmp/oa).
- Fetch KAIYUANSHE reports for 2022–2025.
- Verify CCF ODC.
- Check the Ministry of Civil Affairs 年检 records.

- **Fact:** OpenAtom's donation income is 100% domestic in both years. **Inference:** this contrasts with the Xinhua "¥600M+ since 2020" figure (C): the two filed years total ~¥139M, so the cumulative claim needs the 2020–2021 and 2024–2025 filings to be checked.

## OpenAtom: funding and openness (3 Nov 2026)

**Sources.** OpenAtom's statutory 年度工作报告 (annual-inspection filings to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, printed from zwxt.mca.gov.cn) for 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023. All four are image-only PDFs on https://openatom.cn/information/work. We ran OCR on the server (pdftoppm -r 200, tesseract chi_sim+eng). The text is in `sources/ocr/openatom-20{20,21,22,23}-work-report.ocr.txt`. Each year's totals were cross-checked: income minus expenses equals the change in net assets, or the sub-items add up to the stated total. Evidence is **A (OCR)**: the figures must be re-read on the page image before publication. **No 2024 or 2025 report is published** on the disclosure page (checked 3 Nov 2026). The 慈善中国 and chinanpo.mca.gov.cn search pages are JS-only and were not reachable from our hosts. Coverage gap: 2024–2025.

2023 large payments (20.56M, 21%):
- **Huawei Cloud services for OpenHarmony: 6,485,400.**
- OpenHarmony code hosting: 1.65M.
- Event agency 中青旅联科: 5.91M + 2.24M.
- CCTV.com promotion: 1.42M.
- China National Convention Center (openEuler): 2.86M.

**Rough classification of 2023 spending.**
- About 47% was directly open-source-specific engineering and infrastructure (OpenHarmony, openEuler, ecosystem platform).
- About 24% was events, competitions and campus programmes.
- About 29% went to "other public-interest" activity, mixed.
- Admin was 3.95% of total expenditure.

**Reconciliation with Xinhua's "¥600M+ raised since 2020" (C).** The filed donations for 2020–23 total ¥223.6M; total income is ¥270.5M. Reaching ¥600M by mid-2026 would need about ¥330M more in 2024 to mid-2026, roughly ¥130M a year. That is possible if 2023's growth continued, but no filing supports it. The figure may also count pledges or project donations booked elsewhere, such as the Shenzhen service centre.

### Findings
1. **FACT (A, OCR).** OpenAtom's filed income for 2020–23 is ¥270.5M. Of this, ¥223.6M was donations, all from Chinese companies, with **zero foreign donations in every year**. Spending rose from ¥3.4M (2020) to ¥97.5M (2023). Net assets were about ¥130M at end-2023. No filing exists for 2024–25.
2. **FACT (A, OCR).** OpenAtom also receives **government money**: a ¥1.46M subsidy in 2020 and in 2021, and **¥20.7M in 2023**, of which ¥20.2M was restricted to the 开源项目生态培育平台 (ecosystem cultivation platform). The filings do not name the granting body; MIIT is likely (inference). This is the only part of OpenAtom's income that belongs in public-funding totals.
3. **FACT (A, OCR).** OpenAtom is financially a **Huawei-anchored** vehicle. In 2023, Huawei Device and Huawei Technologies gave ¥27.85M, 37% of all donations. OpenHarmony took 28% of charitable spending, and ¥6.49M of it was paid to **Huawei Cloud**. **INFERENCE:** part of the donated money flows back to the donor as cloud-service revenue. Related-party disclosure covers this, but it is not arm's-length.
4. **FACT (A, OCR).** Roughly half of 2023 charitable spending went to open-source engineering and infrastructure (OpenHarmony, openEuler, the platform). About a quarter went to events, competitions and campus/talent programmes, which promote "open source" but produce no code. Admin overhead is low (3.95%).
5. **FACT (B, repo check).** Every OpenAtom project we checked (35 repos) is published under an OSI-approved licence: Apache-2.0, MulanPSL-2.0, MIT, BSD-3, or GPL-2.0/3.0. MulanPSL-2.0 is OSI-approved. MulanPSL-1.0 and MulanPubL are not, and we found no OpenAtom project using them. Licences for model and robotics projects (Mobius, HaiRuo, OpenLoong…) remain unchecked.
6. **INFERENCE.** "Open source" applies to OpenAtom's **upstream code, not to the products it feeds**:
   - HarmonyOS NEXT is proprietary on top of OpenHarmony.
   - Commercial Kylin, UOS and EulerOS distributions are sold on top of openEuler and openKylin.
   - XTS certification and OpenHarmony device certification are brand and compatibility programmes, not code.
   - The foundation funds the open commons that national-champion commercial stacks depend on.
7. **INFERENCE: classification for data/funding.** Donation records are private corporate philanthropy. Keep them as `instrument_type: donation`, `summable: false`, and exclude them from the government total. They can be shown as a separate "private/foundation OSS funding" line. The **2023 ¥20.7M government subsidy** is public, disbursed and OSS-specific. Record it as a grant via an intermediary (OpenAtom), but leave it `summable: false` until the granting body and the OCR figure are verified on the image. OpenHarmony adoption subsidies (Shenzhen etc.) are recorded separately and must not be double-counted with this.
8. **INFERENCE.** The ¥600M+ Xinhua figure (C) cannot be reconciled with the filings for 2020–23 (¥270M in income). It should be cited only as "reported by Xinhua". Next step: get the 2024/2025 年检 filings from chinanpo.mca.gov.cn via a CN-IP browser.


=== COSCon (China Open Source Conference) themes by year — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/coscon-themes/ ===

# COSCon (中国开源年会), KAIYUANSHE annual conference, 2016–2026

Research note, 2026-11-03. Evidence levels per METHODOLOGY.md §4. KAIYUANSHE's blog posts and annual reports are self-published primary texts. They count as A for event facts (date, venue, theme), and their self-reported figures count as C.
Scope: a light pass with about 25 sources. Track lists are complete only where noted.

| 9 | 2024 | 2–3 Nov (closed 3 Nov) | Beijing; combined with KAIYUANSHE's 10th-anniversary carnival | Open Source, Open Life / 开源新生活 | 10-year review, community, AI | https://blog.csdn.net/kaiyuanshe/article/details/144151303 | A |
| 10 | 2025 | 6–7 Dec | Beijing, Haidian (丽亭华苑 hotel) | 众智开源 / Open Source, Open Intelligence | **open-source AI ("open intelligence")**, 开源集市 (open-source marketplace) with partner booths | https://www.pingwest.com/a/309504 ; https://cloud.tencent.com/developer/news/1226793 | A/B |
| — | 2026 | not found as of 2026-11-03 | — | — | — | — | gap |

The **中国开源年度报告** (China Open Source Annual Report) has been released at or around COSCon since 2015. The 2024 edition is the 10th: https://kaiyuanshe.github.io/2024-China-Open-Source-Report/preface.html (A).

## 2. Comparison: OpenAtom flagship events (state-backed)

| Year | Event | Theme / focus | Source | Ev. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 开放原子全球开源峰会 | not fetched this pass | — | gap |
| 2024 | 开放原子开发者大会暨首届开源技术学术大会 | developers + academia | http://paper.ce.cn/pad/content/202501/01/content_306857.html | B |
| 2025 | 开放原子开源生态大会, 23 Jul, Beijing | 8 new project donations covering AI, embodied intelligence, basic software and blockchain; "全栈协同" (full-stack coordination) | http://www.news.cn/sci-tech/20250725/fad2cf09702c410985ce5318d5c587cf/c.html | B |
| 2026 | 开放原子开源生态大会, 25 Jun, Beijing | 开源赋能产业，生态共筑未来; AI-agent Skills dataset 源图; Anolis (龙蜥) recast as an AI-native OS community; Mulan licence family donated | https://www.news.cn/info/20260625/a9b84c78ac8946c6a7e37bbae91513af/c.html | B |

## 3. Trend analysis (INFERENCE)
1. **Topics change from community to AI.** 2016–2019 topics were community, education, open hardware and "crossing boundaries". 2020–2022 brought "for good", "happy" and "open the world" during COVID. 2025 made AI the theme itself ("Open Intelligence").
2. **COSCon keeps an international frame; the state events stress industry.** COSCon partnered with the ASF in 2020, and its 2019 and 2022 themes are about crossing borders. OpenAtom's 2026 theme is "empowering industry", and the Xinhua report on it does not mention international cooperation.
3. **Governance and compliance are recurring tracks** (2019 community governance, 2021 risk governance). This parallels EU OSPO and supply-chain-compliance work (CRA, OpenSSF, Eclipse ORC WG).
4. **The event is moving to Beijing** (2024, 2025). This may bring it closer to the policy centre; that is speculative.
5. **Gaps:** we have no full track lists for most years and themes for 2016–2017 are only from Qwen (D); 2018 verified (A). Next pass: fetch each year's 议程 page on kaiyuanshe.cn from a CN IP.


=== Industrial open-source stacks in Europe and China — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/industrial-stacks/ ===

# Industrial open-source stacks: EU vs China

Scope decision of 2 Nov 2026: besides public-administration reuse, the observatory tracks how each side builds open-source stacks for its own industry. Records: `data/catalogue-verified.json`, category `industrial-stack` (10 EU, 10 CN). Evidence: A official primary, B reputable secondary, C press. Adoption figures are claims unless stated.

## Table by layer

| Layer | EU | China |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Eclipse Oniro (on OpenHarmony; Eclipse WG) [A] | openEuler (MulanPSL2; claim >16 m installs) [A]; OpenAnolis (Mulan PSL v2, Alibaba-led) [B]; OpenHarmony [B]; Kuanghong coal-mine OS [C] |
| Cloud | Sovereign Cloud Stack [A]; IPCEI-CIS, EUR 1.2 bn public cap [A] | (no dedicated record yet; openEuler/Anolis are the base layer) |
| Edge / IoT | IPCEI-CIS (edge-cloud continuum) [A] | OpenHarmony industrial use [B/C] |
| Automotive | Eclipse SDV / S-CORE [A] | (not yet covered) |
| Chips | DARE RISC-V, EuroHPC, EUR 120 m EU share [A]; RISE (global, LF) [B] | XiangShan (ICT-CAS/BOSC, Mulan PSL v2) [A] |
| AI models | OpenEuroLLM (Digital Europe) [A]; EuroLLM, Apache-2.0 [A] | DeepSeek-R1 (MIT) [A]; Qwen3 (Apache-2.0) [A]; PaddlePaddle (Apache-2.0) [A] |
| Code hosting / foundation | Eclipse Foundation (hosts several stacks above) | OpenAtom Foundation [A]; AtomGit [C] |
| Data spaces | Tractus-X / Catena-X [A]; Gaia-X [B] | (not yet covered) |

## Governance and funding pattern (fact)
- EU: foundations and associations (Eclipse, Linux Foundation, AISBL, e.V.) plus explicit public money (IPCEI-CIS, EuroHPC, Digital Europe Programme).
- China: OpenAtom Foundation as umbrella for OS projects; AI models and several OS distributions are company-led (Alibaba, Baidu, DeepSeek). Public funding is not documented in the sources read.
- Licences: EU stacks mostly Eclipse/Apache; Chinese OS and chip projects use Mulan PSL v2 (permissive, bilingual); Chinese models use MIT/Apache-2.0.

## Cross-participation (fact, sourced)
- Eclipse Oniro was established through collaboration of the Eclipse Foundation and OpenAtom and builds on OpenHarmony.
- Tractus-X lists a China community base; Catena-X's member logo wall includes CATL and Huawei (roles not described).
- EuroLLM supports Chinese as a language (no Chinese contributor documented).

## Complementarity / overlap
- Fact: both sides use RISC-V (DARE vs XiangShan) and both publish open-weight LLMs under permissive licences.
- Inference: overlap is strongest at the OS and RISC-V layers (shared base, different governance); complementarity at data spaces and automotive, where the EU leads with documented governance and China records are missing.
- Inference: Oniro is the existing institutional bridge; permissive licences on both sides (Apache, Mulan, MIT) make upstream code reuse legally low-friction.
- Proposal: add records for Chinese automotive/data-space/cloud stacks and for Gitee; use Oniro and Tractus-X China as case studies for the bridge-opportunity criterion; seek primary sources for the 16 m openEuler claim and for Kuanghong deployments (VPN queue).

## Gaps
Public funding for CN stacks undocumented; licences for several EU entries not stated on pages read; RISE and Gaia-X read only at homepage (B); MindSpore, openKylin (page 404), OpenCloudOS, Gitee, Linux Foundation Europe Open Wallet, Eclipse SDV member list not verified and not recorded.


=== Open-source policy at EU, national, Chinese central and provincial level — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/multilevel-policy/ ===

# Multi-level registry of open-source / digital-commons initiatives: EU and China

Draft v0.1, 2 November 2026. Data: [../data/initiatives.json](../data/initiatives.json) (50 records). Source URLs: [../data/new_source_urls.txt](../data/new_source_urls.txt).
Method: about 40 web calls. Chinese municipal texts for Beijing, Shanghai, Hangzhou, Shenzhen and Chongqing were read in full or in part through the r.jina.ai relay; MIIT only as a press-conference text. Many EU items rest on search summaries. Each record carries an `evidence` grade (primary / secondary / unverified). Targets are announced goals, not results, unless stated.

## (a) Overview

| Level | Records | Primary | What it contains |
|---|---|---|---|
| EU | 12 | 4 | Open Source Strategy (3 Jun 2026), Maintenance Instrument, Open Internet Stack, Commission OSPO and network, DC-EDIC, EDCOM, EU-STF pilot, Interoperable Europe Act/OSOR, NGI, CRA Art. 24, Digital Europe (not researched), JRC (not researched) |
| CN-central | 11 | 6 | MIIT AI+Software plan (11 Sep 2026), 14th and 15th FYP, OpenAtom, AtomGit, Gitee, Mulan, GB/T 44272-2024 (unverified), KAIYUANSHE, OpenHarmony, RISC-V guidance (unverified) |
| EU-national | 15 | 3 | FR La Suite (+ unsourced Etalab stub), DE ZenDiS/openDesk, Sovereign Tech Agency, Deutschland-Stack, Schleswig-Holstein, IT CAD arts. 68-69 + Developers Italia, NL policy and code.overheid.nl, ES CTT, DK, EE X-Road, AT Bundesheer, BE, PL |
| CN-provincial | 12 | 7 | Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Hangzhou, Jiangsu/Suzhou, Guangdong, Shenzhen (+Longgang), Chongqing (plan + foundation), Wuhan, Hunan |

Changes to the memo found while verifying:
- MIIT says "5 or more" key projects by 2028, not "at least five". The text read does not mention SBOM, public-sector adoption or international cooperation.
- Beijing's plan was issued **24 Dec 2025**. It contains no amounts, but it has a procurement-linked instrument ("open-source first solution", support as a share of actual procurement value) and SBOMs "in principle" for fiscally funded software. The memo underplayed this.
- Shanghai: doc no. 沪府办〔2025〕33号, effective 15 Dec 2025 to 14 Dec 2028. No monetary amounts and no procurement or OSPO provisions.
- Hangzhou caps verified: RMB 1m / 500k, plus RMB 2m platform grants. Hangzhou 杭政办函〔2026〕9号, effective 27 May 2026 to 2028.
- Shenzhen: 深府办规〔2026〕1号, 15% + 5%, RMB 10m cap confirmed.
- Jiangsu: the RMB 1bn is "planned total scale"; paid-in status unstated. 16 first tenants.
- Guangdong: no document number; announced at a press conference (year not on page).
- Chongqing: milestones of 20,000 developers by 2027 (new); no amounts.
- New: Wuhan (Jan 2026), explicitly encouraging fiscally funded public-body systems on OpenHarmony (secondary source); Hunan (13 Oct 2026).
- Not found: Sichuan, Fujian, Shandong provincial open-source plans (one search; absence not proven).
- The 15th FYP Outline (13 Mar 2026): no confirmation of an explicit open-source passage. Only the Government Work Report line "support building AI open-source communities" is reported, via secondary press.

## (b) Cross-level comparison

### EU vs China central

| Dimension | EU | China central |
|---|---|---|
| Core instrument | Soft law plus institutions: Strategy, DC-EDIC, EDCOM, OSPO network. Hard law at the edges: Interoperable Europe Act (equivalence-based open-source preference), CRA steward role | Industrial-policy plans (MIIT) that channel projects to one national foundation and one national platform |
| Who funds | Commission grants (NGI, EDCOM, possibly Digital Europe), Member State contributions; Open Internet Stack and the Maintenance Instrument have no amounts yet | No central amounts found in the MIIT text; funding is implicit through OpenAtom and provinces |
| Reuse logic | Reuse of public code and interoperability solutions (portal, OSPO network, procurement guidelines, EUPL) | Reuse of code, models and datasets on AtomGit; reuse as hosting/discovery, not as administrative duty |
| Creation vs maintenance | First explicit maintenance tools: Maintenance Instrument, EU-STF pilot, dependency mapping, CRA stewards | Creation and incubation dominate (key projects, incubation, projects count). Maintenance is not a named instrument in the texts read |
| Governance | Multi-state consortium, subsidiarity, neutrality criteria | One national foundation (OpenAtom) acts as steward and platform owner; independence not assessed |
| Public-sector demand | Procurement guidelines and open-source-first language (weak per CNLL) | Not addressed in the MIIT text read; left to provinces |

### EU national vs China provincial

| Dimension | EU member states | Chinese cities/provinces |
|---|---|---|
| Typical instrument | Platform or institution run by the administration (La Suite, openDesk, code.overheid.nl, CTT), legal duty to publish (IT art. 69, NL "open unless") | Quantified ecosystem targets plus subsidy: project awards (Hangzhou), community operating-cost share (Guangdong), adoption subsidy (Shenzhen), funds (Jiangsu) |
| Who funds | Central government budgets; DINUM seeks ministry contributions; ZenDiS federal; STA federal | City/province budgets; Jiangsu mixes public money and investor funds (announced) |
| Reuse logic | Reuse **between administrations** (same code deployed in many bodies; Docs co-developed FR/DE) | Reuse mostly **between firms and communities** (national hosting required for Hangzhou award); public-sector reuse appears only in Beijing (SBOM, donation to platforms) and Wuhan/Longgang/Chongqing (OpenHarmony systems) |
| Demand side | Sovereignty-driven migration (FR Visio 2027, SH LibreOffice, DK, AT) | Industrial upgrade subsidies (Shenzhen), public-body IoT systems (Wuhan, Chongqing) |
| Maintenance | STA (DE) is the only mature example; most MS programmes build and migrate | Guangdong cost share is the closest analogue; no maintainer-level fund seen |
| Transparency | Usage figures often press/vendor claims, critics exist (Cour des comptes) | Targets only; achieved results rarely reported |

A recurring pattern: Europe's strength is **administration-to-administration reuse and law**; China's is **fast, quantified, multi-instrument local programmes**. Neither side evidences independent outcome data.

## (c) Pairings

| EU / EU-national | China | Fit | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| EU-01 Strategy | CNC-01 MIIT AI+Software | partial | Both make open source industrial/sovereignty infrastructure. EU stresses public administration and maintenance; MIIT stresses incubation and AI |
| EU-05 DC-EDIC | CNC-04 OpenAtom | partial | Stewardship institutions; very different mandate (consortium of states vs. non-profit foundation) |
| EU-12 EU-STF, EUN-DE-02 STA | CNP-HZ, CNP-GD, CNP-JS | weak | Money for open-source work. Hangzhou pays one-off incubation awards, Guangdong pays community operating costs, Jiangsu is venture finance. None funds maintainers of third-party dependencies |
| EUN-NL-01, EUN-IT-01 | CNP-BJ | partial | Only Beijing couples procurement and SBOM with open source in a public text |
| EU-09 CRA / E6 dependency intelligence | CNP-BJ, CNP-SH (SBOM) | partial | Both lean on SBOMs; legal force differs (EU regulation vs municipal plan) |
| EUN-FR-01, EUN-DE-01 workspace suites | CNP-SZ-LG, CNP-WH, CNP-CQ (OpenHarmony in government systems) | weak | Same goal (government systems on open base) but an OS/IoT base is not a document and messaging suite |
| EU-04 OSPO network | CNP-BJ open-source promotion centres | weak | Functional similarity (advice, assessment), no network |

**Pairing is impossible** for: the Interoperable Europe Act (no Chinese interoperability-sharing law found), CAD art. 69 and ENI-style mandatory publication (the earlier OFE-based finding of no formal public-administration reuse policy still holds at national level), the Collaborative Workspace flagship (E5, no equivalent, as in the memo), NGI-type micro-grants (nothing comparable found), CRA stewards (no Chinese legal category found).

## (d) Bridge opportunities at operational level

All are research or evidence exchanges. None implies funding or endorsement, and each is subject to the constraints in memo §8.

| # | Bridge | Level | Actors | Why feasible |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Procurement and SBOM comparison note | EU-national / CN-provincial | Beijing EITB, NL BZK OSPO, Italy AgID | Beijing's text is public and quantifiable; NL and IT have written duties. A desk comparison needs no agreement |
| 2 | Maintenance-funding design comparison | EU / CN-provincial | EU-STF pilot, Sovereign Tech Agency, Hangzhou, Guangdong, OpenAtom | Both sides publish caps/rates; compare grant, cost-share and venture designs and what each leaves unfunded |
| 3 | Public-body OpenHarmony vs open-suite deployments: lessons on adoption barriers | EU-national / CN-provincial | DINUM, ZenDiS, Longgang, Wuhan | Shared problem (moving administrations off proprietary stacks); Cour des comptes critique and Longgang pilot give contrasting evidence. Not a technical exchange |
| 4 | Shared vocabulary for "digital commons" and ownership/non-capture rules | EU / CN-provincial | DC-EDIC (E3), Shanghai Open Source Association, KAIYUANSHE | Shanghai's association already uses digital-commons language; start from the declaration text once obtained |
| 5 | Common reading of state-of-open-source reports | EU / CN-central | E3 State of Digital Commons, KAIYUANSHE China Open Source Report, JRC, OSOR | Both publish; compare metrics and definitions to avoid reading Chinese figures as European-style indicators |
| 6 | Licence and compliance mapping | EU / CN-central | Interoperable Europe/EUPL, OpenAtom, Mulan, GB/T 44272 | Mulan PSL v2 is OSI-approved; EUPL compatibility analysis is a bounded legal task. First verify GB/T 44272 |
| 7 | Eclipse-OpenAtom channel as existing neutral venue | EU / CN-central | Eclipse Foundation, OpenAtom, Oniro | Agreements and sister-project mechanism already exist (S25-S28) |
| 8 | Critical-dependency and project-health metrics | EU / CN-central | E6 dependency intelligence, JRC, OpenAtom/AtomGit, X-lab | Open-data metrics are public; method comparison avoids sharing sensitive data |
| 9 | Conference-level exchange on project-count targets vs outcomes | EU-national / CN-provincial | Italy Developers Italia, Zhejiang, Shanghai | Italy's catalogue gives measured counts, Shanghai/Zhejiang give targets; compare target design and measurement |
| 10 | Education and contribution-credit practice | EU-national / CN-provincial | Austria/Bundesheer upstream contributions, Zhejiang evaluation rules, Chongqing curricula | Zhejiang credits contributions in appraisal; European public bodies could test equivalent practice |
| 11 | X-Road and similar cross-border platforms vs Chinese multi-jurisdiction platforms | EU-national / CN-provincial | NIIS, Shanghai/Hangzhou platforms | Governance of jointly run open platforms; weak evidence on the Chinese side, so scoping first |
| 12 | Open Internet Stack vs AtomGit catalogue design | EU / CN-central | Commission, OpenAtom | Both build a catalogue/hosting layer; compare openness, mirroring and exit rules (mirroring is in the EU Strategy) |

Priority for next work: 1, 2, 4. They rely on published texts, need no data sharing, and match E2, E6/E7 and E3.

## (e) Gaps and unknowns

- **Not verified or not found:** 15th FYP Outline open-source text; GB/T 44272-2024 (title seen only in a listing); CAC and other ministries (nothing found); national RISC-V guidance; Sichuan, Fujian, Shandong; Jiangsu fund paid-in status; Shanghai declaration text; Etalab/French legal base; German OZG; Spain after 2025; Denmark 2026; Estonia, Poland, Belgium country reports (summary only); Digital Europe and JRC (not researched); art. 68 CAD text.
- **EU budgets:** no amount for the Maintenance Instrument or Open Internet Stack; the EUR 2bn / seven years figure is secondary. EDCOM's size and funder are unknown. EU-STF start date conflicts (March vs June 2026).
- **Chinese texts read through secondary reports:** Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Guangdong, Wuhan, Hunan. Official texts would be needed for quotation.
- **Outcome evidence:** neither side offers independent results. Chinese items are almost all targets; French and German adoption figures come from the operators.
- **Structural:** Chinese public-administration reuse remains an open question; Wuhan, Longgang and Chongqing suggest OpenHarmony pilots rather than a reuse regime. Revisit the OFE finding that there is no formal policy.
- **Cautions** (memo §8): export controls, data transfer, dual-use, political sensitivity. Nothing here is an agreed position of the DC-EDIC.


## Round 2 findings (2026-11-02)

Light pass (about 15 searches/fetches). Catalogue now 56 records (added CNC-12..15, CNP-HB-WH, EU-13); notes appended to EU-01, EU-05, CNP-BJ/ZJ/HN.

- **Shanghai September 2026 declaration (priority 1): not found.** Chinese and English searches return only the Dec 2025 Shanghai open-source plan and the 12 Sep 2026 Pudong Innovation Forum. Treat the declaration, including its title, as unconfirmed until a primary text appears. Listed in data/cn_vpn_needed.txt.
- **15th FYP Outline:** Xinhua published the full text on 13 Mar 2026 (18 parts incl. Digital China); the fetched page held only the part list, so no 开源 passage could be confirmed or ruled out. Still open.
- **MIIT:** 4 Sep 2026 AI SME start-up plan 2026-28 (AtomGit, funds for open-source projects); 13 Jan 2026 industrial-internet platform plan (open-source ecosystem goal); on 20 Jul 2026 MIIT said an "AI+software" action plan is coming and 50+ projects are incubating at the national foundation. No joint MIIT/NDRC open-source document found.
- **GB/T 44272-2024: verified** on the SAMR openstd listing (current; published 2024-08-23; effective 2025-03-01). Full text not read.
- **SASAC (new):** Huanxin AI open-source community v2.0, July 2026, China Mobile-led; Feb 2026 directive to central SOEs on open-source communities. Figures are press-only. CAC, MOST, MOE: nothing found.
- **Public-administration reuse:** only secondary English reports on replacing government Windows with Kylin/UOS (openEuler/openKylin as upstreams); no official source, nothing on code sharing between agencies. The no-formal-reuse-regime finding stands.
- **Provinces:** Wuhan (4 OpenHarmony OS, 100k developers by 2027) and Hunan (doc no. 湘制造强省办〔2026〕7号, 13 Oct 2026: 100 scenes, 50k developers by 2028) now have dated targets, still secondary. Sichuan/Chengdu, Fujian, Shandong: nothing found.
- **EU:** strategy is COM(2026) 503. No official budget for the Maintenance Instrument or Open Internet Stack; EUR 350m for an EU-STF is a study/advocacy figure. DC-EDIC (FR, DE, NL, IT, LU; Paris; director from 1 Apr 2026) has no published budget; a Digital Europe EDIC Support Hub call exists (EUR 1m ceiling per an aggregator, to check). CRA: non-binding guidance C(2026) 5252 of 27 Jul 2026 covers FOSS; no separate steward act; reporting duties from 11 Sep 2026, main duties 11 Dec 2027. EU OSPO and EU-STF start date: not researched.
- **Catalogue upgrades (priority 8):** not done beyond the above, for budget reasons.

## Outreach notes
- **Need Chinese (ZH) materials:** 36 entries (CN-central, CN-provincial, CN communities, most CN companies). Use the ZH brief in official register for ministries, community register for KAIYUANSHE, OSChina, Gitee.
- **Need an intermediary (do not cold-contact):** Chinese ministries and provincial bureaus (MIIT, CAC, NDRC, MOST, MOFCOM, SASAC, provincial bureaus): go via KAIYUANSHE, CCF ODC, CAICT, ECNU X-lab, OpenAtom, or the EU Delegation / Chinese Mission. Chinese embassies and the mission: via EEAS or national contacts. Chinese state websites mostly list no generic email; contact_channel is the site's own contact or home page, to be completed by a trusted partner.
- **EU institutions:** official contact forms; for DC-EDIC and EDCOM go through DG CNECT and the Advisory Board secretariat.
- **Member states:** prefer OSPO or digital-agency generic channels; pair each with the matching provincial case ("Beijing <-> Netherlands"). All 27 member states are now covered (BG, HR, CY, GR, HU, IE, LV, LT, MT, RO, SK, SI added 2 Nov 2026; SI: the digital portfolio now sits in the Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration, to confirm).
- **Companies:** use corporate open-source offices, not sales contacts.

## GDPR and approvals
Only institutional channels (generic pages, forms, press offices) are stored. No personal emails, phone numbers, or private social accounts. Named office-holders may be added later only as role + name with a public source. **Every invitation requires Fabio's explicit approval before sending.**

## Link check (automated, 2 Nov 2026)
Home pages reached with HTTP 2xx/3xx: 39 of 111 (field `web_http` in the JSON). Failures are mostly timeouts or bot-blocking from a bulk check (code 0), plus a few 403/404/412 (eu-digit-ospo, eu-itre, ms-fi-dvv, cn-caict, cn-js). They are **not** proof the sites are wrong. Re-check from a normal browser, and from the server for the Chinese sites (see CN-VPN-QUEUE), before any outreach. Pages in contact_channel were not individually fetched.

## Link check (2026-11-02, from the EU server, no tokens)
214 URLs checked (tools/linkcheck.sh): **160 OK (200)**, 22 not found (404), 19 unreachable (timeout or geo-block), 9 blocked (403), 4 other. Failures are in data/stakeholders_linkcheck_fail.tsv. The 404s need the URL corrected; the timeouts on Chinese sites go to the China VPN queue. **A reachable URL does not mean the entry is verified:** organisation, role and contact channel still have to be checked before any outreach.

=== Literature review — https://eu-china-commons.eu/research/literature/ ===

# Literature review: Western work on China's open-source strategy, and what is new in ours

**v0.2 — 2 November 2026.** English. Supersedes the "first search" status of `LITERATURE-AND-NOVELTY.md`.

## 0. Method and limits (read first)

- About 20 web searches/fetches for Task A (cap ~40 for A+B together). Queries used Scholar/SSRN/arXiv-style phrasing plus think-tank names (CSET, Carnegie, DigiChina, ECFR, IFRI, SWP, Clingendael, Bruegel, CEPS, MERICS, Chatham House, OFE, Linux Foundation, OSI).
- **Read in full (text extracted):** MERICS Primer 2021, OFE Country Intelligence Report 2023, House Select Committee letter (June 2025). **Read via fetch-tool summary of the web page (not checked line by line):** Jamestown Parts I and II (Part II page is ~750k characters; only the first 100k were read), China Policy substack, MERICS web page, arXiv 2606.15999 abstract (EconPapers), Gitee OSS-Compass blog.
- **Found but NOT read (snippet only):** Yang 2025 (SAGE), MERICS AI-Stack 2025, OpenUK *AI Openness Report* July 2026 (PDF over 10 MB, fetch failed), Computing.co.uk / Amanda Brock 2026 (HTTP 403), Factsheet China 2023 (PDF text not extractable).
- **Not covered:** Scopus/Web of Science; Google Scholar itself (only web-search proxies); journal-specific searches (*China Quarterly*, *Research Policy*, etc.). CSET, Carnegie, DigiChina, ECFR, IFRI, SWP, Clingendael, Bruegel, CEPS, Chatham House and Rhodium returned **no relevant hit** in the queries run. That is an absence in a limited search, not proof of absence.
- Quotes are under 15 words and come from the fetched text.

## 1. Table of works

## 2. Was the OFE / Interoperable Europe China report updated?

**No update found.** Report dated July 2023; Factsheet metadata 16 Oct 2023. Searches for a 2024-26 update returned nothing. Re-check directly on the Interoperable Europe / OSOR site before asserting this publicly.

## 3. Who comes closest to our work

1. **OFE 2023 and MERICS 2021** are the European precedents: descriptive, pre-dating the EU Open Source Strategy (June 2026) and DC-EDIC, with no mapping of Chinese instruments onto an EU instrument set.
2. **Huawei/Bitergia keynote (Aug 2025)** is the only item found that sets Europe and China side by side and proposes complementarity. Data-led, industry-authored, not policy analysis.
3. **House letter (June 2025)** targets the Eclipse-OpenAtom link we use as a governance case. We must answer it.

## 4. Novelty verdict

**What has been done (evidence above):**
- Security-led readings of OpenAtom, OpenHarmony and openEuler (Jamestown, House, Reuters, ASPI).
- A 2021 EU-side primer with a one-page "Europe should watch" section, and a 2023 EU-commissioned descriptive country profile.
- Chinese-governance analysis (China Policy 2026; Yang 2025) and US-China empirical work on open AI (arXiv 2026).
- An industry-side Europe vs China contribution comparison with a complementarity framing (OSS EU 2025).

**What we did not find, in a limited search:**
- Any mapping of Chinese open-source instruments onto the DC-EDIC Implementation Strategy (adopted 16 Oct 2026, so near-certain).
- Any work scoring fit, feasibility and exposure separately, or using additionality as comparison metric.
- Any instrument-level reading of the 2025-26 regional policies (Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Guangdong/Shenzhen, Chongqing) in a Western language outside our own register.
- Eclipse-OpenAtom treated as a governance case rather than a security alarm.
- An update of OFE 2023.

**Claims in `LITERATURE-AND-NOVELTY.md` to soften:**
- Claim 2 ("a complementarity lens", "no work scores...") is **partly undermined** by item 10 (explicit, numeric complementarity) and by MERICS 2021's opportunities/risks page. Rephrase: "first policy-instrument-level complementarity assessment with separate fit, feasibility and exposure scoring".
- Claim 4 (funding models side by side) is not contradicted, but cite MERICS 2021, which placed the EU OSS Strategy 2020-23 next to Chinese policy.
- "First independent assessment" should read "to our knowledge, in a limited review" until the unread items (OpenUK 2026, Yang 2025, Brock 2026, MERICS 2025, Factsheet 2023, SESEC 2023) are read.

**Could undermine novelty if they contain more than their snippets show:** OpenUK *AI Openness Report* (July 2026; China section plus a UK/European frame) and the SESEC 2023 webinar. Both unread.

**Honest gaps:** no academic-database access; peer-reviewed literature thinly sampled (one hit); Chinese-language and CNKI literature not searched; no direct site searches of Carnegie, CSET, Chatham House; Jamestown Part II mostly unread beyond its first 100k characters.

## 5. Academic databases — PRISMA-style log
